title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: manage workforce requests from Microsoft 365 Copilot chat
summary: Hold: security roles are not the only documented control over the conversational experience. Microsoft also documents Service app deployment and blocking, while the briefing's admin path and Dataverse role-assignment call are valid. The licensing field should acknowledge published product-level requirements without claiming a WEM-specific entitlement is known.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified at 2026-11-21T02:55:45.
The documented WEM catalog contains list_wem_requests, get_wem_request_details and decide_wem_time_off_request.

claims.where: What's changing: Representatives and supervisors do not call the tools directly
claims.claim: Representatives and supervisors interact with the conversational experience rather than calling tools directly.
claims.quote: Customer service representatives and supervisors don't typically use MCP tools directly. Instead, they interact with Service Agent.
claims.fix: Replace 'Representatives and supervisors do not call the tools directly.' with 'Representatives and supervisors do not typically use the tools directly.' This preserves Learn's qualification rather than making the normal interaction pattern categorical.

claims.claim: Service Agent selects and invokes tools in the background and presents results in the conversation.
claims.quote: Service Agent determines which tool to use, invokes it in the background, and presents the result in the conversation.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The Learn overview names Service Agent as an example conversational experience, whereas the roadmap names Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: These tools connect a conversational experience, such as Service Agent, with Dynamics 365 Customer Service and Dataverse so users can complete workforce management tasks through natural language.

claims.claim: list_wem_requests is read-only.
claims.quote: No, listing requests doesn't change data. The request list is read-only.

claims.claim: list_wem_requests displays an interactive list in chat.
claims.quote: The assistant displays an interactive request list as an app-in-chat component.

claims.claim: get_wem_request_details is read-only.
claims.quote: No, viewing a request doesn't change data. The request form is a read-only view of the request's details.

claims.claim: get_wem_request_details opens a single request in an interactive chat card.
claims.quote: The assistant opens a detailed card for a single WEM request. ... The assistant displays an interactive request card as an app-in-chat component.

claims.claim: list_wem_requests defaults to team scope.

claims.claim: Without filters the list covers accessible requests of all types, dates and statuses.
claims.quote: By default, it shows all requests you can access, of every type, across all dates and statuses.

claims.claim: The default maximum result count is 25.
claims.quote: `top` | Integer maximum number of requests to return. Defaults to 25, capped at 200.

claims.claim: The result count is capped at 200.
claims.quote: Integer maximum number of requests to return. Defaults to 25, capped at 200.

claims.claim: Team scope relies on Dataverse and WEM security to return only readable rows.
claims.quote: for the default `scope: team`, it relies on Dataverse and WEM security to return only rows the caller can read.

claims.claim: Time-off request details can include notes.

claims.quote: Shift-bid requests—the request's status, dates, and review information. Shift-swap requests—the request's status, dates, and review information.

claims.claim: Time-off details include the time-off window.
claims.quote: the time-off window for a time-off request, or status, dates, and review information for a bid or swap.

claims.claim: An ambiguous name or agent reference returns matching pending requests instead of guessing.
claims.quote: if your reference matches more than one pending request, it lists the matches and asks you to be more specific instead of guessing.
